_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the single input file x15-rb-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or API was used.

hints.reason: ALIEN via the Toy Story aliens' famous chant of "The claw!" and CRANE via the claw in an arcade crane game; the aliens literally live in a claw machine, so the two sides reinforce each other for a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent indirect pop-culture link; the Toy Story claw machine ties both words together.

hints.reason: ARM is a body limb and BRANCH is a tree limb; a clean, easy double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; LIMB is the natural hint.

hints.reason: BAG because a pouch is a small bag and KANGAROO because joeys ride in the mother's pouch; easy and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward, satisfying easy clue.

hints.reason: BANANA via Donkey Kong's banana hoard and GODZILLA via King Kong's monster battles with Godzilla; two different Kongs, both iconic, makes a fun split.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; banana also evokes gorillas generally, which helps.

hints.reason: BARBIE as the first half of the 2023 double-feature craze and BOMB via Oppenheimer and the atomic bomb; the Barbie side is nearly given away by the portmanteau (it does not literally contain BARBIE), but the bomb side is a satisfying indirect step.

pairs.pair_note: Not literal containment (BARBEN vs BARBIE), but the hint is visibly built from Barbie; flagged uncertain for the owner to decide whether that is too much of a giveaway.

hints.reason: BATTERY via the legal pairing assault and battery, and CHARGE because a military charge is an assault (and assault is a criminal charge); it neatly sidesteps the obvious electrical link between the two words.

pairs.pair_note: Nice misdirection away from electricity; both legal and military senses are accurate.

hints.reason: BILL via "Benjamins" slang for $100 bills bearing Ben Franklin, and BUTTON via The Curious Case of Benjamin Button; two well-known Benjamins give a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: BLOOD flows through veins and GOLD is found in a vein of ore; a clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Solid and accurate.

hints.reason: BOLT via a lightning bolt and FRANKENSTEIN via the iconic film scene where lightning animates the monster; both links are instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the monster's neck bolts add a bonus resonance.

hints.reason: BRAIN via the Scarecrow and HEART via the Tin Man, both seeking gifts from the Wizard of Oz; a classic, satisfying reference.
hints.fix: The Scarecrow and the Tin Man are already in Oz, so the lines should read: "The Scarecrow travels to the Wizard of Oz to ask for a brain." / "The Tin Man travels to the Wizard of Oz to ask for a heart."

pairs.pair_note: Great hint; only the per-word lines need a small wording fix (they live in Oz and go to the Wizard).

hints.reason: CAMP because glamping is a form of camping and LUXURY because it is the luxurious version; it does not literally contain CAMP (G-L-AMP-ING) and reads as a neat definition of the pair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but apt; the portmanteau is exactly camp plus luxury.

hints.reason: CAST via a broken bone in a cast and STAGE via "break a leg" before going on stage; the hidden leg joke links both and avoids the flat theatre route.

pairs.pair_note: Clever: break a leg literally lands you in a cast. Far more fun than a plain theatre hint like PLAY.

hints.reason: GLOVE because a gauntlet is an armored glove and CHALLENGE via throwing down the gauntlet; idiom and object meet in one word.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and satisfying.

hints.reason: CHICK via the peep sound (and marshmallow Peeps chicks) and SHEEP via Little Bo Peep who lost her sheep; a cute two-route aha.

pairs.pair_note: Charming; nursery rhyme plus Easter candy both widely known.

hints.reason: CIRCLE via the circumference-to-diameter ratio and MARCH via Pi Day on 3/14; MARCH is an unexpected partner that clicks nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent indirect link; facts correct.

hints.reason: CLOSET via the wardrobe the children step through and WITCH via the White Witch; the title's "wardrobe" maps naturally to closet for U.S. players.
hints.fix: The children reach Narnia through a wardrobe, a freestanding clothes closet, so the CLOSET line should read: "A wardrobe, a kind of clothes closet, is the doorway to Narnia."

pairs.pair_note: Strong; "wardrobe closet" is slightly loose wording since the book's wardrobe is a piece of furniture.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via booting up and ITALY via its boot shape; a crisp, unexpected double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Good pairing; clearly better use of BOOT than the ITALY + TRUNK version.

hints.reason: CRANE via Dr. Frasier Crane's surname and RADIO via his Seattle call-in radio show; a long-running, recently revived sitcom most U.S. players know.

pairs.pair_note: Good TV link; the CRANE line's "gives his surname to this word" is a little awkward but not false.

hints.reason: CRICKET via the cricket bat and VAMPIRE via vampire bats and bat-shifting vampires; the cricket-as-sport turn is a nice twist since players may first think of the insect.

pairs.pair_note: Cricket bats are familiar enough in the U.S.; fair and pleasant.

hints.reason: SHAPE because a pentagon is a five-sided shape and DEFENSE via the Pentagon housing the Department of Defense; clean and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, solid double meaning.

hints.reason: Both DIAMOND and SKY come from the instantly familiar Beatles title Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds; a phrase-join, but a famous one that pairs the two words exactly.
hints.fix: The DIAMOND line is awkward; suggested: "The full Beatles title is Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds."

pairs.pair_note: Acceptable phrase-join: the song title contains exactly these two words and is iconic.

hints.reason: DRESS via Marilyn Monroe's billowing white dress and SUBWAY via the subway-grate breeze in The Seven Year Itch; one iconic image holds both words.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent scene-based hint; facts correct.

hints.reason: EAR via Spock's pointed Vulcan ears and MIND via the Vulcan mind meld; both are mainstream Star Trek knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: Strong character hint.

hints.reason: A clock has a FACE and HANDs; easy, but it neatly reroutes two body-part words to an object.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, satisfying classic; low delight is fine.

hints.reason: FARM via the nursery song about Old MacDonald's farm and HAMBURGER via McDonald's; a fun aha, though the song's standard spelling is MacDonald.
hints.fix: Old MacDonald (often written McDonald) had a farm, and McDonald's is the world's best-known hamburger chain.

pairs.pair_note: Spelling mismatch with the song (MacDonald) is minor since players hear the name, but the text should acknowledge it; owner may prefer to accept the variant as-is.

hints.reason: FIRE via tinder as fire-starting material and MATCH via a match on the Tinder app; the fire-starting sense of match makes the misdirection extra satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent modern double meaning.

hints.reason: FROST because frosting a cake is icing it and HOCKEY via the icing call; a crisp double meaning that dodges the weather sense of frost.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the rule summary is simplified but fair.

hints.reason: GROUND via ground chuck and WOOD via woodchuck and the famous tongue twister; a phrase-join, but both are instantly familiar and the groundhog/woodchuck echo adds a bonus.
hints.fix: Ground chuck is ground beef made from the chuck, a cut from the shoulder.

pairs.pair_note: Good phrase-join; the GROUND line calls chuck a cut of ground beef, which slightly inverts it (chuck is the cut, ground chuck is the ground beef).

hints.reason: HOLE via the rabbit hole into Wonderland and MIRROR via Through the Looking-Glass; both books' entry points are widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; both portals in one character.

hints.reason: ITALY via its boot shape is strong, but TRUNK only connects through the British word for a car trunk, which the rubric treats as British-only usage for a U.S. audience.

pairs.pair_note: Explanation is true, but the TRUNK side depends on British usage; many Americans know "car boot" from TV, so a second opinion is reasonable. BOOT is better spent on COMPUTER + ITALY.

hints.reason: NOODLE because spaghetti is a noodle and KISS via the Lady and the Tramp spaghetti kiss; a famous scene makes the aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong and accurate.

hints.reason: MARCH via St. Patrick's Day on March 17 and STAR via Patrick Star of SpongeBob; two famous Patricks give a fun split.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent and accurate.

hints.reason: MILITARY via colonel as an officer rank and SECRET via Colonel Sanders' secret blend of herbs and spices; the text correctly avoids claiming Sanders was a military colonel.

pairs.pair_note: Clever indirect route to SECRET; facts correct.

hints.reason: NEW YORK via the Big Apple and WATCH via the Apple Watch; easy, familiar and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but satisfying.

hints.reason: PAINTING because paintings are done on canvas and SAIL because canvas is the traditional sailcloth; both accurate and fair.

pairs.pair_note: The sail side takes a moment but is well known.

hints.reason: PIRATE via Captain Hook and RIGHT via the right hook punch; RIGHT is a tricky partner that clicks once boxing comes to mind.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the RIGHT side is a familiar compound.

hints.reason: PUZZLE via the jigsaw puzzle and TOOL via the jigsaw power saw; the puzzle is named after the saw, so the double meaning is genuine.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning.

hints.reason: TEAM via Marvel's superhero team and REVENGE via avenging; a proper name (not a plural of a target) that honestly links both.

pairs.pair_note: Solid pop-culture link; shares a root with REVENGE but does not contain it.

hints.reason: VALENTINE via Cupid as the Valentine's Day symbol and SANTA via Cupid the reindeer; the reindeer side is a lovely surprise.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent two-holiday hint.

hints.reason: SMOKE and WHITE via the white smoke signalling a new pope (and the pope's white garments add a second route to WHITE); widely known and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Good; the 2025 conclave keeps it fresh.

hints.reason: SOUND via sonic meaning relating to sound (sonic boom) and VIDEO GAME via Sonic the Hedgehog; easy and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean double meaning.

hints.reason: SUN via the solar corona and VIRUS via coronaviruses, both named for a crown; accurate science with a nice shared-etymology payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; pandemic association is mild and handled neutrally.

hints.reason: TOOTH via the dentist's drill and WELL via drilling a well; both are common uses of the word.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, accurate.
